Black-throated Tit

काळ्या गळ्याचा टीट

Aegithalos concinnus

The Black-throated Tit is a very small woodland bird with a bold dark throat patch and an active, sociable manner. It often travels with other birds, moving through branches and leaves as the group searches for food.

About the bird

How to recognise the Black-throated Tit

A dark throat bib and eye mask are useful features to look for. Many populations also have a warm chestnut-toned crown, pale cheeks and contrasting colours around the head and neck.

Plumage varies across its range, so the exact pattern is not identical everywhere. Its small size, rounded body and flocking behaviour provide helpful clues alongside the head markings.

Natural habitat

The places where it lives

It lives in hill forest and woodland, including broadleaved forest, pine woodland and scrubby forest edges. It is usually associated with wooded country rather than open plains.

Groups move through the vegetation as they feed, and may join mixed flocks of other small woodland birds. Some populations change elevation with the season.

Food habits

What it eats and how it feeds

Small insects and spiders form an important part of its food. It also takes some seeds, berries and other plant material.

Birds search among leaves, twigs and branches, picking up small items as they move. Following the progress of the flock is often easier than keeping one individual in view.

Where it occurs in India

Where you may find it in India

In India, the Black-throated Tit is associated mainly with the Himalayan foothills and hill regions, including northern and northeastern parts of the country. It occurs in suitable wooded areas across this broad belt.

It is not a typical bird of the lowland plains or most of peninsular India. Elevation, forest cover and local geography influence where it can be found.
